places.rationale: Rich, high-trust, well-run state with abundant clean power and strong AI uptake; the main drags are a fast-aging population, very low fertility and the long Russian border.

reading.reason: Productivity: a skilled, AI-heavy workforce and an effective state turn automation into output; the Russian border keeps stability from scoring higher.

places.rationale: One of the poorest and least governed places on Earth, in conflict for over a decade with tiny electricity and water access; even modest growth is uncertain and renewed war could halve living standards.

reading.reason: Prices: cheap solar, medicine and food could help, but almost no AI access, no ownership and armed groups that can use new tools cancel it.

places.rationale: Oil-dependent with modest, declining reserves, maximal water stress and rising Gulf heat; a stable monarchy and diversification plans soften but do not remove the risk of decline as oil rents fade.

reading.reason: Ownership: cheap energy erodes the oil rents that fund living standards and Oman owns little compute; cheaper desalination and goods help.

places.rationale: Rich, young and peaceful with very high AI use, but its income leans on US multinationals' taxes and back-office jobs, and it imports most of its energy.

reading.reason: Productivity: among the highest AI use anywhere; the risk is jobs, as Dublin's support, sales and fund-admin work is easy to automate.

places.rationale: Converging EU economy built on car assembly, with fast aging, a populist drift and a border with Ukraine; EU membership anchors the upside.

reading.reason: Jobs: the car-assembly model that made Slovakia is what robots replace, offset by EU-wide productivity gains and cheaper goods.

places.rationale: Occupation, the Gaza war and political paralysis dominate; rebuilding from a depressed base could lift living standards, but further displacement or the collapse of the Palestinian Authority is a real risk.

reading.reason: Stability: AI-enabled surveillance and targeting concentrate power over Palestinians; cheap solar and desalination help only if politics allows.

places.rationale: Rich, stable, isolated food exporter with the highest Claude use here; remoteness and a food surplus make it unusually resilient to global catastrophes, though productivity growth has long been weak.

reading.reason: Productivity: very high AI use and strong institutions; its food and tourism exports are hard to automate, so jobs are spared.

places.rationale: Poor desert Sahel state with mining, fishing and new gas, better governed than its neighbours but highly exposed to heat, drought and jihadist spillover from Mali.

reading.reason: Prices: cheap energy, food and medicine matter most for a poor importer with little AI use; it owns none of the gains.

places.rationale: Stable democracy with clean power, broad health coverage and diversified exports, but rising drug violence and a heavy interest bill; its shared-services sector is exposed to AI.

reading.reason: Jobs: shared-services and call-centre exports are prime AI targets, offset by good AI use, clean power and cheaper imports.

places.rationale: Rich on oil and a huge sovereign fund, but almost wholly dependent on hydrocarbons, among the hottest places on Earth, and two-thirds of residents are low-paid migrants.

reading.reason: Ownership: oil rents fall as energy gets cheap, offset by a sovereign fund that holds global equity, AI firms included.

places.rationale: Canal, logistics and finance hub with high inequality and a heavy interest bill; drought on the canal's lakes and fiscal stress are the main risks.

reading.reason: Jobs: banking and back-office services are exposed, but canal trade and copper gain from an AI-driven physical build-out.

places.rationale: Fast-growing tourism and transit economy, but the government's authoritarian turn, a frozen EU path and Russian occupation of a fifth of the territory put stability at risk.

reading.reason: Stability: an authoritarian drift plus AI surveillance and a hostile Russia can undo the gains that good AI uptake would bring.

places.rationale: EU and euro member converging fast on tourism, with severe aging and emigration; Mediterranean heat is the main physical risk.

reading.reason: Productivity: EU-level AI access lifts output, and tourism is in-person work AI does not replace, so jobs are spared.

places.rationale: One of the most closed dictatorships, with indefinite conscription, mass emigration, no economic data for a decade and war risk with Ethiopia; a post-Isaias transition could go either way.

reading.reason: Ownership and stability: a closed regime with almost no internet captures no AI gains and can turn control tools on its people.

places.rationale: Landlocked mineral exporter between China and Russia; copper demand helps while coal exports fade, and harsh winters, water stress and corruption are the drags.

reading.reason: Jobs and exports: copper sells well in an AI-driven build-out and little labour is exposed; China's dominance limits ownership.

places.rationale: Stable, well-governed democracy with clean power and farm and software exports; aging, low fertility and the 2023 water crisis are the main concerns.

reading.reason: Productivity: high AI use and strong institutions; software exports are at risk but farm exports and stability hold.

places.rationale: Already near rich-world consumption thanks to federal transfers, but the population is shrinking and aging fast, the grid is fragile and hurricanes are intensifying.

reading.reason: Ownership: as a US territory it can share in taxes on US AI firms; pharma manufacturing and service jobs are exposed.

places.rationale: Ethnic division, weak governance, emigration and aging hold it back; EU accession is the main upside and Republika Srpska secession the main risk.

reading.reason: Prices: cheaper goods and energy help most, but low Claude use, no ownership and fragile politics limit what else it gains.

places.rationale: Stable democracy with uranium, lithium, diamonds and green-hydrogen potential, but extreme inequality, high hunger and severe drought exposure.

reading.reason: Prices: cheap energy and food help a water-stressed country; uranium and lithium exports gain, but it owns none of the AI.

places.rationale: Tech-minded small economy that has just made peace with Azerbaijan, but water stress, heavy dependence on Russia and a fragile peace weigh on it.

reading.reason: Stability: a fragile peace and Russian leverage matter more than AI; IT outsourcing jobs are exposed to automation.
